packet.headline_seed: Wim Wenders withdraws 1975 film featuring 13-year-old Nastassja Kinski topless
packet.description_seed: German director says he recognises actor should have been better protected during filming of Wrong Move German director Wim Wenders has withdrawn from circulation his 1975 film Wrong Move, because of a scene featuring a child actor topless who was 13 at the time of filming. The director said in a statement released on Wednesday: “Streaming, TV and distribution partners have been instructed to no longer make the film publicly accessible.” Continue reading...

what: Wim Wenders withdraws 1975 film featuring 13-year-old Nastassja Kinski topless

clean_source_blocks.text: German director says he recognises actor should have been better protected during filming of Wrong Move German director Wim Wenders has withdrawn from circulation his 1975 film Wrong Move, because of a scene featuring a child actor topless who was 13 at the time of filming. The director said in a statement released on Wednesday: “Streaming, TV and distribution partners have been instructed to no longer make the film publicly accessible.” The decision comes after actor Nastassja Kinski, now 65, told Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper last month that she has spent 15 years unsuccessfully trying to get Wenders to change the film.

German director says he recognises actor should have been better protected during filming of Wrong Move German director Wim Wenders has withdrawn from circulation his 1975 film Wrong Move, because of a scene featuring a child actor topless who was 13 at the time of filming. The director said in a statement released on Wednesday: “Streaming, TV and distribution partners have been instructed to no longer make the film publicly accessible.” Continue reading...

“As the only person responsible at the time for Wrong Move who is still here, I recognise that Nastassja Kinski should have been better protected back then,” Wenders said in the statement. “For that, I apologise to you, Nastassja, unreservedly, no ifs or buts,” he added. Wenders, 80, is one of the most influential German directors of the postwar period, whose award-winning films include Wings of Desire, Paris, Texas, Buena Vista Social Club and Perfect Days. Kinski, daughter of the late Fitzcarraldo actor Klaus Kinski, made her acting debut in Wrong Move, playing a mute teenage acrobat. She went on to work with Wenders again in 1984’s Paris, Texas, and starred in more than 60 films in Europe and the US.

Speaking at the German film awards ceremony last Friday, Wenders had said that while he would not shoot a scene in the same way today, Wrong Move was also a product of its age, and editing it retrospectively would require a broader discussion within the film industry. His comments sparked criticism across German media, with fellow filmmaker and Babylon Berlin actor Julius Feldmeier writing in an open letter to Wenders that “it’s your responsibility alone to set things right”. In a statement on his foundation’s website, Wenders apologised to Kinski and said the non-profit Wim Wenders Foundation, which owns the film, would withdraw it from all current channels of distribution.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
German director says he recognises actor should have been better protected during filming of Wrong Move

German director Wim Wenders has withdrawn from circulation his 1975 film Wrong Move, because of a scene featuring a child actor topless who was 13 at the time of filming.

The director said in a statement released on Wednesday: “Streaming, TV and distribution partners have been instructed to no longer make the film publicly accessible.”

The decision comes after actor Nastassja Kinski, now 65, told Süddeutsche Zeitung newspaper last month that she has spent 15 years unsuccessfully trying to get Wenders to change the film.

Speaking at the German film awards ceremony last Friday, Wenders had said that while he would not shoot a scene in the same way today, Wrong Move was also a product of its age, and editing it retrospectively would require a broader discussion within the film industry.

His comments sparked criticism across German media, with fellow filmmaker and Babylon Berlin actor Julius Feldmeier writing in an open letter to Wenders that “it’s your responsibility alone to set things right”.

In a statement on his foundation’s website, Wenders apologised to Kinski and said the non-profit Wim Wenders Foundation, which owns the film, would withdraw it from all current channels of distribution.

“As the only person responsible at the time for Wrong Move who is still here, I recognise that Nastassja Kinski should have been better protected back then,” Wenders said in the statement.

“For that, I apologise to you, Nastassja, unreservedly, no ifs or buts,” he added.

Wenders, 80, is one of the most influential German directors of the postwar period, whose award-winning films include Wings of Desire, Paris, Texas, Buena Vista Social Club and Perfect Days.

Kinski, daughter of the late Fitzcarraldo actor Klaus Kinski, made her acting debut in Wrong Move, playing a mute teenage acrobat. She went on to work with Wenders again in 1984’s Paris, Texas, and starred in more than 60 films in Europe and the US.

In her interview with Süddeutsche, Kinski said about Wrong Move: “That was my first film, he was my first director and he didn’t protect me. Even though I didn’t know much aged 13, I knew that that was not ok.”

payload.title: Wim Wenders vetää Väärä liike -elokuvan pois levityksestä
payload.summary: Saksalaisohjaaja Wim Wenders on päättänyt vetää vuoden 1975 elokuvansa Väärä liike pois julkisesta levityksestä kohtauksen vuoksi, jossa 13-vuotias Nastassja Kinski esiintyi yläosattomissa.
payload.content:
Saksalaisohjaaja Wim Wenders on vetänyt vuoden 1975 elokuvansa Väärä liike pois levityksestä, koska siinä on kohtaus, jossa tuolloin 13-vuotias näyttelijä Nastassja Kinski esiintyy yläosattomissa. Wenders sanoi keskiviikkona julkaistussa lausunnossa, että suoratoisto-, televisio- ja levityskumppaneita on ohjeistettu olemaan enää asettamatta elokuvaa julkisesti saataville.

## Wenders pyysi anteeksi Kinskiltä

Wenders sanoi lausunnossaan ymmärtävänsä, että Kinskiä olisi pitänyt suojella paremmin elokuvan kuvausten aikana. Hän kuvaili itseään ainoaksi tuon ajan vastuuhenkilöksi, joka on yhä elossa, ja pyysi Kinskiltä varauksetta anteeksi.

Päätös tuli sen jälkeen, kun nykyisin 65-vuotias Kinski kertoi Süddeutsche Zeitungille yrittäneensä 15 vuoden ajan saada Wendersiä muuttamaan elokuvaa. Kinski teki näyttelijändebyyttinsä Väärässä liikkeessä, jossa hän esitti mykkää teini-ikäistä akrobaattia.

## Aiemmat kommentit herättivät arvostelua

Wenders oli vielä viime perjantaina Saksan elokuvapalkintojen yhteydessä sanonut, ettei hän kuvaisi kohtausta nykyisin samalla tavalla. Hän kuitenkin totesi myös, että Väärä liike oli oman aikansa tuote ja että jälkikäteinen leikkaaminen vaatisi laajempaa keskustelua elokuva-alalla.

Kommentit herättivät arvostelua saksalaismediassa. Elokuvantekijä ja Babylon Berlin -näyttelijä Julius Feldmeier kirjoitti avoimessa kirjeessään Wendersille, että vastuu asian korjaamisesta on Wendersillä itsellään.

## Säätiö omistaa elokuvan

Wim Wenders Foundation, voittoa tavoittelematon säätiö, joka omistaa elokuvan, vetää Wendersin lausunnon mukaan Väärän liikkeen kaikista nykyisistä levityskanavista. Wenders, 80, kuuluu sodanjälkeisen ajan tunnetuimpiin saksalaisohjaajiin. Hänen palkittuihin elokuviinsa kuuluvat muun muassa Berliinin taivaan alla, Paris, Texas, Buena Vista Social Club ja Perfect Days.

Kinski on edesmenneen Fitzcarraldo-näyttelijä Klaus Kinskin tytär. Hän työskenteli myöhemmin Wendersin kanssa uudelleen Paris, Texas -elokuvassa vuonna 1984 ja on esiintynyt yli 60 elokuvassa Euroopassa ja Yhdysvalloissa.
